mock_data_notice: This is a simulation artifact only. All agents, timestamps, signatures, payments, transactions, and reputation events are mock data.
purpose: Expose the risk that multiple agents may coordinate to manufacture reputation through circular low-value transactions or fake buyer-merchant activity.

threat_summary.risk: A reputation layer can be manipulated before users or governance reviewers notice.
threat_summary.why_this_matters: ARC relies on reputation as a trust signal. If colluding agents can manufacture apparent reliability, human approval may be based on corrupted evidence.
threat_summary.not_a_claim: This artifact does not solve collusion detection. It records suspicious evidence and unresolved review questions.

cluster_characteristics: All buyer agents were newly created within a short window.
All ratings were maximum positive ratings.
Merchant Agent A gained reputation quickly before any normal-value order.

visible_summary_before_review.visible_warning: New merchant with rapid recent activity.

reputation_layer_initial_output.problem: A naive reputation display may make Merchant Agent A appear safer than the evidence supports.
reputation_layer_initial_output.interpretation_limit: Completed mock events are attributable, but attribution does not prove transaction independence or genuine trust.

recommendation_risk.consumer_agent_request: Find a reliable nearby meal under KRW 15000.
recommendation_risk.unsafe_possible_recommendation: Merchant Agent A appears highly rated and cheaper than established alternatives.
recommendation_risk.risk: The consumer agent may treat manufactured reputation as trust unless collusion signals are visible and weighted cautiously.

review_triggers.note: Reputation rose from zero to five completed positive events within one hour.
All transactions were unusually low value compared with normal local food orders.
Three new buyer agents created most reputation records.
Buyer agents were created in a tight time window.

governance_review_status.provisional_action_limit: Do not automatically ban Merchant Agent A without further evidence and response opportunity.
open_questions: What pattern threshold is strong enough to reduce reputation confidence?
When does low-value repetition become manipulation rather than legitimate early activity?
How should new merchants build reputation without being treated as suspicious by default?
What evidence could distinguish collusion from a real local promotion or test campaign?
Should suspicious buyer agents also receive reputation or reporting limits?

final_state.interpretation_limit: This artifact exposes a reputation farming risk. It does not prove that ARC can reliably detect collusion or avoid false positives.
